decisions.statement: A transient transport error is a TypeError whose message has a known phrase.
An idle timeout abort is transient where the message has the idle token.
A DOMException with no idle timeout token is not transient.
A retry happens only for a transient transport error.
The backoff list has one wait for each retry.
An error surviving the last backoff wait is rethrown to the caller.
An operation handed to the retry must be safe to run more than once.
The sleep is handed in so a test needs no wait.
Nothing here retries on an upstream status.
A bare error code matches only where the message has that code as a whole word.
A TypeError message with `instanceof` is not a transient transport error.
The first chunk of an upstream body is read before the wrapper is handed back.
The wrapper copies each upstream chunk into a second ReadableStream.
The re-wrap costs 87% of the streaming CPU a live gateway spends.
Downstream backpressure never reaches the upstream reader.
A slow downstream reader grows the wrapper's queue to the whole upstream body.
A null upstream body stops the idle guard.
A failure reading the first chunk is thrown to the caller rather than framed.
A failure reading the first chunk reaches the observer as an upstream error.
A failure reading the first chunk stops the idle guard.
Each chunk that arrives resets the idle guard.
Each chunk that arrives resets the keepalive emitter.
A keepalive emitter is built only where the keepalive interval is above zero.
A keepalive comment goes out only where the last byte sent was a newline.
Each path the wrapped stream ends by stops the keepalive emitter.
Each path the wrapped stream ends by stops the idle guard.
Each path the wrapped stream ends by releases the upstream reader.
A downstream cancel is passed on to the upstream reader.
The cancel is the last word a cancelled stream gives the observer.
A cancel while a read is pending sends the pump's close down the error path.
A mid-stream failure is served as an SSE error frame only where the caller asked.
A served frame is opened with a newline where the last byte sent was no newline.
A mid-stream failure the caller wants no frame for errors the wrapped stream.
A stream closed by a served error frame reports no completion.
An observer callback that throws is swallowed before the throw reaches the pump.
The clock is handed in so a test needs no real time.

definition: an upstream connection break either side of the first chunk of a response
